newsitem.title: MEXICO: Carso Q2 shows Sears turnaround begins.
newsitem.headline: Carso Q2 shows Sears turnaround begins.

text.p: Second quarter earnings reported by Mexican conglomerate Grupo Carso showed a smaller impact than expected from its absorbing loss-making store chain Sears Roebuck de Mexico, analysts said.
Carso posted net earnings for the second quarter of 622.5 million pesos, compared with an average of 625 million forecast by analysts in a previously conducted Reuters survey.
Analysts said improved earnings by the cigarette division, Cigatam, helped offset losses by Sears.

"Carso's earnings were basically decent, and slightly better than expected overall. Cigatam exceeded our expectations, but there were no other surprises," said Kerry McHugh, an equity analyst with Goldman, Sachs & Co.
Cigatam cut prices on its leading Marlboro brand in March by 20 percent to combat smuggling of cheaper Marlboro cigarettes from the United States, a move that ate into Carso's first-quarter earnings.
For Robert Hulme, of Interacciones brokerage, second quarter numbers for Cigatam showed "volumes are beginning to offset the price cut."

Cigatam posted operating earnings of 318.1 million pesos for the second quarter, up from 215.5 million for this year's first quarter. The division's operating margin rose to 24.6 percent from 19.6 percent compared with the same period.
Alexander Ryshawy focused instead on early signs that Carso had managed to turn Sears around.
"The bright spot is Sears, which posted an operating profit for June," he said.
Carso had bought an estimated 82 percent of retailer Sears Roebuck de Mexico from its U.S. parent Sears, Roebuck and Co during the quarter.
Ryshawy added that Sears had improved its operating margin to negative seven percent in the second quarter from minus 17.5 percent in the first quarter.
"Cost-cutting is showing immediate benefits," he said.
McHugh said the early improvement in Sears showed the group could recover from its acquisition in the near future.
"Carso took a big writeoff this quarter. Sears tells us operating margins will be better in the future," she said.
Hulme, however, said "We expected sales to rise and margins to fall because of Sears; but sales actually fell, which shows there are still problems elsewhere," he said.
Net sales for the second quarter totaled 6.637 billion pesos, down from 6.669 billion pesos in the previous quarter and below analysts' forecast of 7.039 billion pesos.
"There were not the type of gains seen in other conglomerates, such as Alfa (SA ) and Desc (Sociedad de Fomento Industrial SA de CV ), which had much better quarters," Hulme added.
Hulme noted, however, a conference call hosted by Carso on Wednesday morning suggested that "financially, acquisitions and disposals look interesting."
Carso expected $400 million during the current quarter from a previously agreed sale of a stake in Cigatam to Philip Morris Cos Inc, he added.
